macros.name: circleclasses
macros.doc: This command is a lot like \structline except that it puts a circle around the classes instead of connecting them with a line.

macros.name: class
macros.doc: This places a class at (x,y) where x and y are integers.

macros.name: classoptions
macros.doc: This adds options to an existing class.

macros.name: Do
macros.doc: The \Do command is less general than \foreach; the purpose is to provide a syntax for stack-based looping that is similar to \DoUntilOutOfBounds but with a fixed range. So \Do{n}\marg{loop body} repeats ⟨loop body⟩ n times.

macros.name: doptions
macros.doc: This command adds options to an existing differential, just like \classoptions except for differentials.

macros.name: DrawIfValidDifferential
macros.doc: Test whether a differential is valid.

macros.name: extension
macros.doc: The \extension command has an identical syntax to the \structline command and most of the same options. Instead of adding a structline, it adds an extension.

macros.name: extensionoptions
macros.doc: This command adds options to an existing extension.

macros.name: getdtarget
macros.doc: Sets \⟨macro⟩ equal to the coordinates of the target position of a length ⟨page⟩ differential starting at ⟨source coordinate⟩.

macros.name: IfAliveF
macros.doc: Test whether a class is alive on the given page.

macros.name: IfAliveT
macros.doc: Test whether a class is alive on the given page.

macros.name: IfAliveTF
macros.doc: Test whether a class is alive on the given page.

macros.name: IfExistsF
macros.doc: Test whether a class of the given description exists.

macros.name: IfExistsT
macros.doc: Test whether a class of the given description exists.

macros.name: IfInBoundsF
macros.doc: Test whether a class is in bounds or out of bounds.

macros.name: IfInBoundsT
macros.doc: Test whether a class is in bounds or out of bounds.

macros.name: IfInBoundsTF
macros.doc: Test whether a class is in bounds or out of bounds.

macros.name: kill
macros.doc: This command sets the indicated coordinate to die on the indicated page, but does not establish a target for the differential.

macros.name: lastclass
macros.doc: The command \lastclass evaluates to the coordinate of the most recent class on the stack.

macros.name: lastx
macros.doc: The commands \lastx and \lasty evaluate to the x and y position, respectively, of the nth class on the stack.

macros.name: lasty
macros.doc: The commands \lastx and \lasty evaluate to the x and y position, respectively, of the nth class on the stack.

macros.name: nameclass
macros.doc: The \nameclass command gives a name to a class.

macros.name: printpage
macros.doc: This command prints a single page of an existing spectral sequence as-is.

macros.name: pushstack
macros.doc: This adds a class to the top of the stack.

macros.name: replaceclass
macros.doc: Using the command \replaceclass causes a new symbol to appear on the page after a class supported or accepted a differential (or both).

macros.name: replacesource
macros.doc: The variants \replacesource and \replacetarget replace the source and target respectively of the most recent differential.

macros.name: replacetarget
macros.doc: The variants \replacesource and \replacetarget replace the source and target respectively of the most recent differential.

macros.name: SseqErrorToWarning
macros.doc: Turns the error with the given name into a warning.

macros.name: SseqIfEmptyF
macros.doc: This tests if an expression is the empty expression.

macros.name: SseqIfEmptyT
macros.doc: This tests if an expression is the empty expression.

macros.name: SseqIfEmptyTF
macros.doc: This tests if an expression is the empty expression.

macros.name: SseqNewClassPattern
macros.doc: Creates a new class pattern.

macros.name: SseqNewFamily
macros.doc: This makes a new family with name ⟨family name⟩.

macros.name: SseqNormalizeMonomial
macros.doc: This command simplifies a monomial by combining like variables and removing bases that are raised to the 0th power, removing exponents of 1, removing 1’s, and replacing the empty monomial with 1.

macros.name: SseqOrientationNormal
macros.doc: \SseqOrientationNormal indicates that the content is normal (not rotated).

macros.name: SseqOrientationSideways
macros.doc: \SseqOrientationSideways indicates that the content is rotated 90 degrees (it doesn’t matter in which direction).

macros.name: SseqParseInt
macros.doc: Stores the result of evaluating an integer expression into \⟨macro⟩.

macros.name: sseqset
macros.doc: The \sseqset command is for adjusting the global options for all spectral sequences in the current scope, or for applying options to the rest of the current spectral sequence.

macros.name: structline
macros.doc: The \structline command creates a structure line from ⟨source coordinate⟩ to ⟨target coordinate⟩.

macros.name: structlineoptions
macros.doc: This command adds options to an existing structure line, just like \classoptions except for structure lines.

macros.name: tagclass
macros.doc: The \tagclass command gives a tag to a class.

envs.name: sseqdata
envs.doc: The {sseqdata} environment is for storing a spectral sequence to be printed later.

envs.name: sseqpage
envs.doc: The {sseqpage} environment can also be used to print a stand-alone page of a spectral sequence – that is, if you only want to print a single page of the spectral sequence, you can skip using the {sseqdata} environment.
